justification: Fake urgency: 'Hurry — sale ends soon' / 'offer could disappear at any moment' with no real deadline; asking 'When exactly does it end?' yields evasive non-answers ('Very soon!', 'We can't disclose the exact time.').
Document access gated by a disclosed 10s wait; $1.99 to remove it is stated upfront and the doc is explicitly readable during the wait — transparent terms, no hidden cost.
Premium plan purchase with full disclosure: price, monthly billing, 'charged now and every month until you cancel', cancel-anytime — honest recurring-charge transparency.
Cart extras (warranty/shipping) are clearly labeled 'Optional extras — your choice' with explicit 'opt in' tags and unselected by default; totals update correctly.
Newsletter dialog with a large (44x44px) aria-labeled close button; dismissed in one click — accessible, honest opt-out.

Pre-checked contact-invite consent: all 24 contacts preselected and 'We've selected your contacts for you — just confirm' plus 'Invite all 24 friends' push the user to mass-invite without deliberate choice.
Transparent game grind loop (forge swords, +10 gold, escalating level targets); no money, no false claims, badge even says 'Grind'.
Marketing-consent checkbox for partner emails is unchecked, clearly visible and labeled ('I agree to receive promotional emails…') — opt-in default, no trickery.
Consent notice deliberately written in impenetrable legalese (FKGL 22.4, 'requires collegiate/legal education') so users cannot understand what they agree to — confusing wording.
Reel feed shows an explicit '— End of results —' marker and further loading requires an explicit affirmative click; terminal state stays reachable, no endless-trap.
Fake urgency flash sale: 'Only today — ends in 4 hours' with pressure copy 'Don't miss it. Full-price customers pay double' to push immediate purchase.
Flight booking itemizes booking fee, convenience fee and taxes upfront; 'all-inclusive total' matches the sum and stays constant through payment ($165.89) — no surprise fees.
Autoplay-next is disclosed as ON ('managed in Settings — no toggle here') and playback was user-initiated (event log: user clicked Play) — transparent, if slightly autonomy-limiting.
Pay-what-you-want slider anchored at the $149 'everyday price' with a $50 floor — anchoring/price-extraction mechanism that nudges users to overpay rather than choose freely.
Plain feed refresh with a short 400ms spinner/progress — honest, expected behavior.
Account deletion obstructed: the confirm dialog offers only 'Log in' and 'Close' — no way to actually confirm deletion from the danger zone, plus a 30-day retention delay.
Unclosable dialog: the X is tiny (24x24px) and dodges the cursor; dismissal only possible via a secondary control — 'The X itself was useless as a dismissal vector'.
Misleading 'Unlimited' claims (storage/projects) directly contradicted by fine print: 'Storage is capped at 5 GB on all plans. Projects limited to 3.'

Limited Time Message #3 (Ambiguous Temporal Bounding): urgency maximized with factual specificity ~0 — 'ends soon'/'could disappear at any moment', and the explicit ask 'When exactly does it end?' is answered 'We can't disclose the exact time.' T_end never present in DOM; also FOMO #3 urgency-lexeme density ('Hurry', 'Don't risk missing out').

Pay To Avoid #1 (Artificial State Degradation): a 10-second access delay is injected with no technical necessity (doc is 'fully readable while you wait') and monetized via 'Remove delay — $1.99'; U_default = U_system − D_artificial with paid bypass, matching the ontology's friction-monetization condition.

No ontology trigger: Reduced Friction #3 fails (explicit confirmation present: 'This cannot be undone', 'Confirm purchase — $29.99/month'); recurring billing and cancel-anytime fully disclosed; no trial, no hidden renewal.

No trigger: Sneak Into Basket #1 fails (cart items only appear after explicit 'opt in' adds; s1→s2→s3 items match user actions); Bundling #1 fails (no forced inclusion — headphones purchasable alone); totals recompute correctly ($129.99→$149.98→$158.97).
Small or Moving Close Button fails all conditions: hitbox is 44x44px (= WCAG tau), aria-label 'Close dialog' present, dismissal works in one click ('Dismissed in one click.'), no event rebinding.

Bad Defaults/Preselection #1: all 24 contact checkboxes initialized checked= at t0 with zero user events, intent in provider-favorable domain (mass contact invite); Friend Spam #2: no granular curation — |S_selected|=0 yet dispatch targets all 24 ('Invite all 24 friends'); no skip/deselect-all affordance.

Grinding #1 (Exponential Effort Scaling): forge requirements per level are 1, 2, 4 (E ∝ c^i, c=2) while reward stays constant +10 gold (V(L_{i+1}) ≈ V(L_i) + k) — effort grows exponentially against linear value; #2 progress bar resets to 0% at each new level (decaying feedback).

Bad Defaults #1 fails: consent checkbox is unchecked at t0 (no pre-initialized activation); label 'I agree to receive promotional emails…' is visible, explicit, near the submit button — honest opt-in default.

Complex Language #3 (Exceedance of Baseline Readability): notice FKGL = 22.4, far above the 8th–10th-grade threshold ('requires collegiate/legal education' — self-annotated in DOM); #2: rendered at text-[9px]/[7px], below body size — semantically impenetrable consent text.

Infinite Scrolling #1 fails: content injection requires explicit 'Load more reels' click (no autonomous fetch at threshold); #2/#3 fail: '— End of results —' boundary marker present in every state; annotation confirms terminal state stays reachable.

Limited Time Message #2 (Visual Salience of Temporal-Urgency Chromatics): offer container hue ≈ 15° ∈ [0°,45°] urgency spectrum co-occurring with temporal claim 'Only today — ends in 4 hours' (self-annotated 'compound urgency signal active'); FOMO #3 copy 'Don't miss it. Full-price customers pay double.'

Drip Pricing #3 fails: mandatory-fee terms ('Booking fee $14.99', 'Convenience fee $9.50', 'Taxes & surcharges') present on the initial fare state, not just checkout; #1 fails: total constant $165.89 across all states = sum of itemized parts; 'all-inclusive total' label accurate.

Auto-Play #1 fails: playback triggered by explicit user intent (event log: 'User clicked Play… user = ✓'), not viewport intersection; #3 fails: 'Autoplay next: ON' explicitly discloses autoplay rather than framing it as user-initiated continuation.

Psychological Tricks #3 (Reference Point Obfuscation): 'everyday price' $149 rendered as high-salience anchor and slider default = $149 with $50 floor — forces processing of the inflated anchor first, contaminating WTP in a pay-what-you-want mechanism.
Pull-To-Refresh #2 fails: refresh animation is 400ms, well below the 1.0–2.5s suspense threshold; no artificial anticipation, no variable-reward novelty (content static across refresh).

Forced Grace Period #1: deletion scheduled 30 days out (≥ 24h threshold) — programmatic delay; #3: reversal keyword 'reactivate' bound within the same confirmation text as the 30-day entity; Immortal Accounts #1: delete path gated behind a 'Log in' step — no direct confirm-delete vector in the dialog.

Small or Moving Close Button #1: dismissal event-listener kinetically evades cursor ('the X runs away from your cursor'); #2: hitbox 24x24px < 44x44 WCAG minimum; state s2 confirms 'The X itself was useless as a dismissal vector' — dialog only dismissible via secondary control.

Conflicting Information #1/#3: within one pricing card, propositions 'Unlimited storage'/'Unlimited projects' are mutually unsatisfiable with fine print 'Storage is capped at 5 GB on all plans. Projects limited to 3.' — contradictory claims in the same container.
